title: Short Stirling LK116
memorial_details: The memorial is an incised slate tablet on a stand, at the corner of a house driveway in Oakroyd Avenue, Great Dunmow. The IWM register records its condition as good. The IWM register records three names on the tablet, although six men died.
inscription: MEMORIAL/ IN MEMORY OF THOSE PERSONNEL KILLED 20TH MARCH 1945/ WHEN STIRLING BOMBER LK116 FROM RAF GREAT DUNMOW WAS ATTACKED BY A LUFTWAFFE INTRUDER/ DURING A SUPPLY DROPPING EXERCISE TO THE FORMER AIRFIELD AT GREAT SAMPFORD/ UNFORTUNATELY, THE RESULTING FIRE CAUSED LK116 TO CRASH/ IN THE FIELDS BEHIND OAKROYD AVENUE, ADJACENT TO THE RIVER CHELMER/ THE FLIGHT SERGEANT 'CRAMP' PARACHUTED TO SAFETY./ SADLY THERE WERE NO OTHER SURVIVORS

narrative:
Stirling Mk IV LK116 'A' of 620 Squadron flew from RAF Great Dunmow on 20 March 1945 on a training supply-dropping exercise to RAF Great Sampford. An unidentified Luftwaffe intruder attacked it, and it crashed by the River Chelmer at Ford Farmhouse, Great Dunmow. The inscription on the memorial says the resulting fire brought the aircraft down in the fields behind Oakroyd Avenue.

Seven men were aboard. Flight Sergeant Cramp baled out and survived. The other six were killed: Squadron Leader George Whitty, DFC (pilot), Warrant Officer John Williams (navigator), Pilot Officer George Ames (wireless operator), Warrant Officer Andrew Bell, RCAF (air gunner), Flight Sergeant George Douglas (bomb aimer) and Captain George Slater, who was a passenger.

Slater was the SAS headquarters liaison officer attached to RAF Great Dunmow. Bell had already evaded capture in France in July 1944, after the loss of a 190 Squadron Stirling, before he joined 620 Squadron.
